thresholds.ci: The `@ci` test opens four representative models: the basic Stroop reference, EGO in each of its views (nested, flattened, PyTorch) and with CIMs shown, MontagueDayanSejnowski96 (learning), and `demos/nested_compositions.py` (a composition open inside another). In every view it requires all of show_graph's nodes on the canvas, rows and order at 100%, no overlapping boxes, nothing cut off after Fit, no frame button covered, and every edge show_graph draws between two canvas nodes drawn along its course (no exceptions are listed). Measured with the full batch: all of those pass at 100%. The full batch below has no thresholds; it is run before a release and its review sheets looked at.

why.Giallanza2024_ego_study2.py — Flatten (a: Not a layout difference: after the batch folds EGO's compositions in the flattened (or PyTorch) view, the canvas stops being laid out Like show_graph. None of show_graph's edge courses is drawn (0 of 31) and the boxes sit in the Layered stand-in's arrangement, while the same views measured before folding agree 100%. The later variants of the flattened view inherit that state. Likely the show_graph placement no longer fits the graph after a fold in the flattened view; not yet confirmed.
